title: progressive-degradation-customer-communications-and-postmortem-draft
summary: Template and working draft for customer-facing updates and postmortem summary for incidents characterized by progressive degradation of inference latency and increased error rate.
subject_lines: Service degradation impacting inference latency — update and mitigation

status_page_snippets: Detected: We are investigating reports of increased latency and transient errors impacting the Redwood hosted API. Some requests may experience delays or failures. Our engineers are actively diagnosing the issue and will post updates every 30 minutes.

Mitigation in progress: We have identified a traffic-pattern regression affecting batching heuristics on a subset of models. A temporary routing change has been deployed to reduce request volume to impacted nodes while a targeted patch is validated. Error rate and latency are improving for most customers; we continue to monitor and will follow up with a full summary.
Resolved: A fix was deployed and validated. Normal performance has been restored across regions. We will publish a detailed postmortem with root cause analysis and next steps within 72 hours.
content:
Purpose:
This document is a living draft intended for customer-facing communications in incidents where performance degrades progressively (rising tail latency, intermittent 5xxs) rather than a single catastrophic outage. It includes suggested status page updates, email subject options, an external postmortem skeleton, and guidance for accounts teams handling high-touch customers. Use this as a starting point and customize the technical detail based on the customer’s SLA and security posture.

Situation overview (short):
- Impact: Beginning 2026-08-27 21:07 UTC, Redwood observed a gradual increase in request latency and a rise in transient 500/502 errors for our hosted API for a subset of model-serving pools. The degradation was progressive — errors and higher p99s appeared first for long sequence requests, then broadened to shorter sequences. No data exfiltration or security compromise detected.
- Scope: ~7% of overall requests (weighted by token usage) experienced >2x latency increase at peak; error rate for affected pools peaked at ~6%. Impacted customers include those pinned to model variants with larger KV-cache footprints and open-loop streaming patterns.
- User impact classification (customer-facing): Degraded performance leading to timeouts and slower responses; some retries required. Not all customers affected.

Suggested immediate status page updates (timeline style):
- T+0 (first update): "We are investigating reports of increased latency and transient errors affecting parts of the Redwood hosted API. Some requests may experience delays or failures. Our engineers are actively investigating. Relevant teams notified"
- T+30–60: "Root-cause hypothesis: regression in batching/cache heuristics in the serving runtime caused poor CPU/GPU kernel selection under certain sequence-length distributions. We are validating a configuration roll-back and a routing change to move traffic off impacted nodes. Customers will see partial improvement during the next 10–20 minutes"
- T+120: "Mitigation deployed: automated routing changes in place and a patch validated on canary pools. Error rate dropping and tail latency improving; monitoring closely for regressions. We will publish a full incident report within 72 hours."

Draft short email/update to customers (when quick direct note needed):
Subject: "Update: Intermittent latency and errors affecting Redwood hosted API"
Body:
Hi —
We wanted to let you know we’re currently investigating intermittent latency and error responses affecting a portion of Redwood hosted API requests. Our engineers have identified a likely cause related to runtime batching and cache behavior under specific workloads and are deploying mitigations now. You may see improved responses in the next 10–30 minutes.
We’ll post another update as we validate the fix. If you have high-priority traffic that must not be affected, please reply to this message and we will coordinate temporary routing/pinning.
Thanks for your patience,
Asha (Customer Success) on behalf of the incident team

Postmortem summary (customer-facing) — skeleton to fill in:
Title: Customer-facing incident summary — progressive performance degradation on hosted API (2026-08-27)
Summary (one paragraph):
On 2026-08-27 we observed a progressive performance degradation in Redwood’s hosted API that resulted in increased request latency and a rise in transient 5xx errors for a subset of model-serving pools. The issue affected roughly 7% of requests by token usage and primarily impacted customers using long-sequence workloads and certain model variants. Normal service was restored after a targeted routing change and a runtime configuration rollback; a permanent patch was rolled out the following day. No customer data was exposed.
Root cause (concise, non-technical + optional technical annex):
- Customer-facing phrase: A recent runtime change to batching and cache heuristics caused the inference runtime to make suboptimal kernel and memory decisions for certain sequence-length distributions, which increased processing latency and led to retries and transient errors.
- Technical annex (for customers with engineering contacts): The runtime’s continuous batching heuristics incorrectly prioritized batching parameters when concurrent long-sequence streams were present, which triggered a path that selected a fallback kernel with higher latency on affected GPU types. This, combined with eviction behavior on the KV cache, amplified tail latency under load.
Mitigation and remediation steps taken:
- Immediate: throttled and rerouted traffic away from impacted pools, applied a configuration rollback to batching heuristics, and increased canary coverage for the fix.
- Short term: deployed a targeted patch to the serving runtime to correct kernel selection logic and altered cache eviction thresholds for long sequences.
- Long term: added production tests that exercise mixed sequence-length traffic patterns, added alerting on specific p99 biomarkers (per-model p99 delta > 30%), and updated rollout gates for runtime changes to include staged model/seq-length validation.
Customer impact & compensation guidance:
- Impact: Customers with workloads using long sequences or streaming-style patterns may have experienced slower responses and transient failures. Most customers saw improvements within 2 hours; full resolution occurred after the patch next-day.
- Recommended customer outreach: For accounts impacted above the SLA threshold, offer a credit per the SLA terms. For strategic accounts, propose a dedicated post-incident review with engineering and an implementation plan for request-level routing controls.
Follow-up items (public-facing commitments):
- Publish technical postmortem within 72 hours with timelines and logs redacted as necessary.
- Share the rollout plan for modified runtime heuristics and the expanded QA plan.
- Proactively notify customers using models known to be sensitive to sequence-length distributions when runtime changes are scheduled in the future.

Account-team playbook (quick bullets for CSMs/AMs):
- Step 1: Use the status page snippets above to send one brief update within 30 minutes. Keep tone calm, factual, and action-oriented.
- Step 2: Identify customers on pinned model variants or with heavy long-sequence usage (query query-ids: top-10 by token-rate).
- Step 3: For customers showing errors above 1% of their requests, offer manual routing/pinning to a stable pool and open a support priority queue.
- Step 4: After resolution, schedule an account review and offer a written postmortem (redacted technical annex) and potential credits if SLA thresholds were breached.

Guidance on technical detail level (pick one depending on the customer):
- High-level only: explain that we had a runtime behavior regression and have fixed it; emphasize no data exposure and the roadmap to avoid recurrence.
- Engineering to engineering: include kernel selection description, EV/kv cache behavior, JIRA/PR numbers, and a link to the technical postmortem.

Unresolved questions & investigation items (for internal hand-off):
- Why did our canary and staging traffic not trigger the regression? (Investigation ticket: INC-4321)
- Confirm whether a particular GPU type (A100 vs H100) showed higher susceptibility and add to compatibility matrix.
- Verify if any customer-side retry logic amplified load causing cascading effects.

Suggested internal tags and routing for the postmortem: incident, perf-regression, serving-runtime, batching, kv-cache, priority:high.

Notes to editor:
- Keep the customer-facing postmortem to one page where possible; move deep technical timelines and logs to a separate annex or internal-only Confluence page.
- Templates above should be localized for high-touch enterprise customers (more technical detail, offer of joint RCA call) vs. broad-status updates (concise, non-technical).

Draft sign-off checklist (before publishing customer-facing postmortem):
- Tech lead (serving-runtime) has approved the root-cause wording: YES/NO
- SRE has validated metrics and dashboards: YES/NO
- Legal/security cleared (no sensitive log data to be published): YES/NO
- Product/CS review for customer tone and compensation guidance: YES/NO

Appendix: Example short timeline (fill with actual timestamps during incident):
- 2026-08-27 21:07 UTC — first anomaly alert (p99 increase on pool X)
- 2026-08-27 21:18 UTC — on-call triage; initial mitigation plan formed
- 2026-08-27 21:40 UTC — traffic routing change deployed to reduce load on pool X
- 2026-08-27 22:10 UTC — error rate reduced but tail latency still elevated for long sequences
- 2026-08-28 03:15 UTC — permanent patch merged to runtime; staged rollout begins
- 2026-08-28 08:30 UTC — patch validated; full rollback of temporary routing; monitoring shows sustained return to baseline

End of draft. Use this as the canonical customer-facing template for progressive performance degradations. Replace placeholders and timestamps with verified incident data before publishing.
postmortem_summary: Public one-paragraph summary ready for publication: On 2026-08-27 Redwood experienced a progressive degradation in hosted API performance that temporarily increased latency and errors for a subset of customers. We deployed routing mitigations and rolled out a runtime patch; normal service was restored and a full technical postmortem (with remediation and testing changes) will be shared within 72 hours. No customer data was exposed.
